narrative.overview: The House List renders as a working architectural drawing: a deep-navy canvas ruled with a faint measurement grid, with each real thing on the list pinned to it as a paper spec sheet. The system exists to make a financial tradeoff legible in seconds, not to decorate a todo list. Every device serves that: the budget bar reads as a dimension line rather than a progress ring, prices set in tabular monospace so figures compare cleanly down a column, and priority is a paper title-block tab rather than a colored dot. This is an Operate-mode surface (a tool used mid-decision, not browsed for pleasure), so the system deliberately refuses ornament: no kickers, no icon-plus-heading feature cards, no gradient text. Color is functional throughout — red/amber/blue never appear as decoration, only as the priority or status they name, and always paired with a text label so the system never depends on color alone.
keyCharacteristics: Dark drafting-table canvas (ruled grid) as permanent chrome; content lives on paper-toned cards pinned to it.
Monospace for every price, date, tag, and room name — data reads as data, distinct from prose.
A dimension-line budget bar, not a progress bar or a KPI tile.
Every priority color is paired with a text label; never color alone.
Calm, flat, and quiet — the system's only job is legibility under a real spending decision.

rules.name: Never-Color-Alone
rules.body: Every priority is a text badge, never a bare color swatch or dot.

rules.name: Surface-Tuned Ink
rules.body: A priority's saturated swatch is never used as body text directly; each color carries separate variants tuned per surface (soft-tint ink, on-navy bright/dark, and a darkened solid for white button text) rather than one color reused everywhere.

rules.name: Mono-Is-Data
rules.body: Monospace marks measurement (prices, dates, tags), never prose.

rules.name: Paper-Lifts
rules.body: Only surfaces literally pinned to the canvas (cards, dialogs, the FAB) carry a shadow; the canvas, header, and budget-bar panel stay flat.

dos: Do pair every priority color with its text label — badge, filter chip, or status text. Never a bare swatch.
Do use monospace exclusively for measured data (prices, dates, tags) — never for prose.
Do use the 7px solid priority tab on any new card-like surface that carries a priority; keep it a full-height tab, not a thin accent border.
Do reach for the surface-tuned ink/bright/dark variant whenever a priority or status color is used as text; never the bare saturated swatch.
Do keep the canvas flat and reserve shadow for surfaces literally pinned on top of it.
donts: Don't add a kicker/eyebrow label above a heading anywhere in the system.
Don't use a hard-edged, zero-blur neobrutalist shadow anywhere.
Don't introduce a second accent color — someday blue is the only non-semantic accent.
Don't render a priority/status color as body text without checking which surface it's on.
